''See also: [[gate (The Traveler's Gate Trilogy) Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|A Gate serves as a [[portal]] or opening that connects the primary world to various different Territories. These openings are manipulated and controlled by individuals known as [[Travelers]], who can summon them using specific gestures, words, or physical items. The appearance and behavior of a Gate vary significantly depending on the [[Territory]] it connects to; for example, an [[Endross Gate]] may manifest as a small, concentrated thunderstorm in a person's palm that grows in size and power the longer it remains active. Other [[Gates]] might appear as swirling doorways with specific colored edges, such as blue for [[Asphodel]] or red for [[Tartarus]] and [[Naraka]]. While many [[Travelers]] can open these portals at will, certain [[Gates]] are subject to unique restrictions. A [[Valinhall Gate]] typically requires a full [[Traveler]] utilizing an assigned [[Dragon's Fang]] to remain open, and these portals generally return the user to their original starting location. Some specific [[Gates]], such as those leading to the [[Crimson Vault]], can only be opened from within the primary world rather than from within a [[Territory]]. Because [[Gates]] can be used to follow [[Travelers]] into foreign lands, specialized tools called gatecrawlers exist. These devices are capable of prying open a Gate shortly after it has been closed, allowing an individual to track or pursue a [[Traveler]] into another realm. Managing and opening these portals can be physically demanding, often requiring significant effort and strength from the user.}}

== House of Blades ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|A Gate serves as a [[portal]] or defensive structure that creates an opening between the world and a [[Territory]]. While [[Leah]] used one to transport people, [[Travelers]] possess the ability to dissipate these openings at will. During a confrontation, [[Simon]] managed to tear open a Gate by reaching through his sword toward [[Valinhall]], though the aperture steadily shrunk as it sealed itself. In another instance, a Gate leading to a red cavern manifested before [[Malachi]]. Because of the danger involved, [[Travelers]] will attack [[Simon]] if they witness him attempting to open a Gate for [[Traveling]].}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|A Gate serves as a means of travel between different Territories, potentially opening onto a clearing or near a [[Hanging Tree]]. While these portals can be cut open, they require significant strength to operate, and the [[frozen horn]] possesses the power to close them. During one instance, a Gate manifested in midair with crackling white edges that revealed a deep green forest. [[Leah]] utilized such a [[portal]] to return home, whereas [[Simon]] found himself unable to stop long enough to open one. Additionally, a Gate was known to lead directly into a room within the royal palace in [[Cana]].}}

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|During the events in the [[City of Light]], it is established that a [[Helgard Incarnation]] lacks the ability to open a Gate leading to a different [[Territory]]. [[Leah]] demonstrates a unique capability by being able to shove individuals through a Gate. Amidst the chaos, an angry [[red Gate]] appears behind a giant, and [[Indirial]] potentially vanishes into one. Ultimately, the Gate is seen as being clean and white.}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|An angry [[red Gate]] is behind the giant.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c14">''City of Light'', chapter 14</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Indirial]] may have vanished into a Gate.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c21">''City of Light'', chapter 21</ref>}}</li>
